title: Liguria's Diesel Prices Just Fell Off a Cliff
dek: While gasoline keeps creeping upward across the region, Liguria's self-service diesel price posted its sharpest single-day drop in more than a week.
body: In Liguria today, self-service Benzina sits at €2.0149 per liter and self-service Gasolio at €2.0817. That puts local gasoline about 1.6 cents above the national self-service average of €1.9989, while diesel has swung the other way — now roughly 1.8 cents below the national average of €2.0995. A region that was tracking above the national line on both fuels a week ago is now split: pricier gas, cheaper diesel.

The two fuels have been telling very different stories all week. Benzina has climbed almost every single day, up from €1.9685 on July 21 to today's €2.0149 — a steady 2.4% gain with barely a pause. Gasolio followed the same upward path through July 27, peaking near €2.2106, then reversed hard: it dropped more than 12 cents per liter overnight into today, a 5.5% single-day fall that erased over a week of gains in one move. Meanwhile the local station network stayed steady, with 491 of Liguria's 539 registered stations reporting prices today, one more than yesterday.

Catching a swing like that — a double-digit-cent overnight move in one region, while the fuel next to it keeps climbing — is only possible because this dashboard rebuilds itself from the national MIMIT feed every day without anyone manually re-pulling spreadsheets.
